parole.significato: any plant of the Abrus taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Abrus, from Ancient Greek ἁβρός (habrós, “delicate”).

parole.significato: synonym of sapodilla
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Achras, from Ancient Greek ἀχράς (akhrás).

parole.significato: any insect of the Aphodius taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Aphodius, derived from Ancient Greek ἄφοδος (áphodos, “latrine, shitter”).

parole.significato: any moth of the taxonomic genus Aglaope
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Aglaope, derived from Ancient Greek ἀγλαός (aglaós, “splendid, shining”) + ὤψ, ὠπός (ṓps, ōpós, “appearance”).

parole.significato: any member of the Anabaena taxonomic genus
parole.testo: From translingual Anabaena, from Ancient Greek ἀναβαίνω (anabaínō, “I go up”).

parole.significato: any member of the extinct Anaspida taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Anaspida, derived from Ancient Greek ἀν- (an-, “not", "without”) + ἀσπίς (aspís, “shield”).

parole.significato: any salamander of the Andrias taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Andrias, from Ancient Greek ἀνδριᾱ́ς (andriā́s, “image of a man, statue”).

parole.significato: any tree of the Aristotelia taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Aristotelia, derived from Ancient Greek Ἀριστοτέλης (Aristotélēs, “Aristotle”).

parole.significato: any fern of the Blechnum taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Blechnum, from Ancient Greek βλῆχνον (blêkhnon).

parole.significato: any member of the Blenniidae taxonomic family
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Blenniidae, derived from Blennius, derived from Ancient Greek βλέννα (blénna, “mucus”).

parole.significato: Blennius, taxonomic genus of fish
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Blennius, derived from Ancient Greek βλέννα (blénna, “mucus”).

parole.significato: bee fly
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Bombylius, from Ancient Greek βομβυλιός (bombuliós, “a buzzing insect; (by extension) a narrow-necked vessel”).

parole.significato: sideroxylon
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Bumelia, derived from Ancient Greek βουμελία (boumelía, “ash”, tree).

parole.significato: caterpillar hunter (any ground beetle of the genus Calosoma)
parole.testo: From translingual Calosoma, derived from Ancient Greek καλός (kalós, “beautiful”) + σῶμα (sôma, “body”).

parole.significato: any seaweed of the Caulerpa taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Caulerpa, from Ancient Greek καυλός (kaulós, “stem”) + ἕρπω (hérpō, “I crawl”).

parole.significato: any cephid, particularly of the species Cephus pygmaeus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Cephus, from Ancient Greek κηφήν (kēphḗn, “male bee”).

parole.significato: any protozoan of the genus Ceratium
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Ceratium, from Ancient Greek κεράτιον (kerátion), diminutive of κέρας (kéras, “horn”).

parole.significato: any member of the Ceroplastes taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Ceroplastes, from Ancient Greek κηροπλάστης (kēroplástēs).

parole.significato: any parasite of the Chlamydozoon taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Chlamydozoon, derived from Ancient Greek χλαμύδιον (khlamúdion, “small cloak”) + ζῷον (zōîon, “animal”).

parole.significato: any fish of the Chlorophthalmus taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Chlorophthalmus, derived from Ancient Greek χλωρός (khlōrós, “pale green”) + ὀφθαλμός (ophthalmós, “eye”).

parole.significato: any fly of the Chlorops taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Chlorops, derived from Ancient Greek χλωρός (khlōrós, “pale green”) + ὤψ (ṓps, “appearance”).

parole.significato: whitefish
parole.testo: From translingual Coregonus, from Ancient Greek κόρη (kórē, “pupil of the eye”) + γωνία (gōnía, “angle”).

parole.significato: any member of the Corydalis taxonomic genus
parole.testo: From translingual Corydalis, from Ancient Greek κορυδαλλίς (korudallís).

parole.significato: any member of the Crambe taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Crambe, from Ancient Greek κράμβη (krámbē, “cabbage”).

parole.significato: any plant of the genus Chrysobalanus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Chrysobalanus, from Ancient Greek χρυσοβάλανος (khrusobálanos, “nutmeg”), derived from χρυσός (khrusós, “gold”) + βάλανος (bálanos, “acorn”).

parole.significato: any plant of the Desmodium taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Desmodium, from Ancient Greek δεσμός (desmós, “bond”).

parole.significato: any plant of the Dicentra taxonomic genus
parole.testo: From translingual Dicentra, from Ancient Greek δίκεντρος (díkentros, “having two stings”).

parole.significato: any plant of the Dicypellium taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Dicypellium, derived from Ancient Greek δι- (di-, “two”) + κύπελλον (kúpellon, “cup”).

parole.significato: Venus flytrap (Dionaea muscipula)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Dionaea, from Ancient Greek Διωναία (Diōnaía), a name of Aphrodite.

parole.significato: any parasite of the Diplozoon taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Diplozoon, derived from Ancient Greek διπλόος (diplóos, “double”) + ζῷον (zōîon, “animal”).

parole.significato: any member of the Dyscophus taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Dyscophus, from Ancient Greek δύσκωφος (dúskōphos, “deaf”).

parole.significato: any rodent of the Echimys taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Echimys, derived from Ancient Greek ἐχῖνος (ekhînos, “hedgehog”) + μῦς (mûs, “mouse, rat”).

parole.significato: any cactus of the Echinocactus taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Echinocactus, derived from Ancient Greek ἐχῖνος (ekhînos, “hedgehog”) + translingual Cactus.

parole.significato: Silvery mole-rat (Heliophobius argenteocinereus)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Heliophobius, derived from Ancient Greek ἥλιος (hḗlios, “sun”) + φόβος (phóbos, “fear”) (hence “fearing sunlight”).

parole.significato: any deciduous tree of the Entandrophragma taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Entandrophragma, derived from Ancient Greek ἐντός (entós, “inside”) + ἀνήρ, ἀνδρός (anḗr, andrós, “man”) + φράγμα (phrágma, “fence, screen”).

parole.significato: any cactus of the Epiphyllum taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Epiphyllum, derived from Ancient Greek ἐπί (epí, “upon”) + φύλλον (phúllon, “leaf”).

parole.significato: Any in the genus Epilachna of beetles.
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Epilachna, derived from Ancient Greek ἐπί (epí, “upon”) + λάχνη (lákhnē, “woolly hair”).

parole.significato: phacelia
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Phacelia, derived from Ancient Greek φάκελος (phákelos, “bundle, faggot”).

parole.significato: any plant of the Phaius taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Phaius, from Ancient Greek φαιός (phaiós, “grey”).

parole.significato: synonym of epifillo
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Phyllocactus, derived from Ancient Greek φύλλον (phúllon, “leaf”) + translingual Cactus.

parole.significato: galium (plant in the Galium genus)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Galium, from Ancient Greek γάλιον (gálion).

parole.significato: wistaria, wisteria
parole.testo: From translingual Glycine, derived from Ancient Greek γλυκύς (glukús, “sweet”).

parole.significato: any fungus of the Gliocladium taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Gliocladium, derived from Ancient Greek γλία (glía, “glue”) + κλάδιον (kládion), diminutive of κλάδος (kládos, “branch”).

parole.significato: any plant in the Gnaphalium taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Gnaphalium, from Ancient Greek γναφάλλιον (gnaphállion, “cottonweed”).

parole.significato: any plant of the Hieracium taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Hieracium, derived from Ancient Greek ἱεράκιον (hierákion).

parole.significato: Any member of the genus Lathyrus.
parole.testo: From translingual Lathyrus, from Ancient Greek λάθυρος (láthuros).

parole.significato: leucojum
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Leucojum, from Ancient Greek λευκόιον (leukóion), derived from λευκός (leukós, “white”) + ἴον (íon, “violet”).

parole.significato: lygodium (fern of the genus Lygodium)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Lygodium, derived from Ancient Greek λυγώδης (lugṓdēs, “willow-like”).

parole.significato: the widelip orchid (Liparis)
parole.testo: From translingual Liparis, from Ancient Greek.

parole.significato: synonym of andria
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Megalobatrachus, from Ancient Greek μεγάλος (megálos, “great, large”) + βάτραχος (bátrakhos, “frog”).

parole.significato: any member of the Melanerpes taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Melanerpes, derived from Ancient Greek μέλανος (mélanos, “black”) + ἕρπω (hérpō, “I crawl”).

parole.significato: any bryozoan of the Myriozoum taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Myriozoum, derived from Ancient Greek μυρίος (muríos, “countless, innumerable”) + ζῷον (zōîon, “animal”).

parole.significato: numbat (Myrmecobius fasciatus)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Myrmecobius, derived from Ancient Greek μύρμηκος (múrmēkos, “ant’s”), genitive of μύρμηξ (múrmēx, “ant”), + βίος (bíos, “life, living”) (hence “living off ants”).

parole.significato: a musk deer
parole.testo: From translingual Moschus, from Ancient Greek μόσχος (móskhos, “musk”).

parole.significato: any member of the genus Nemalion of algae.
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Nemalion, derived from Ancient Greek νῆμα (nêma).

parole.significato: obelia
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Obelia, derived from Ancient Greek ὀβελός (obelós, “spit, rod”).

parole.significato: paspalum (plant of the genus Paspalum)
parole.testo: From translingual Paspalum, from Hellenistic Ancient Greek πάσπαλος (páspalos, “type of millet”).

parole.significato: a plant in the genus Pedalium: Pedalium murex
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Pedalium, from Ancient Greek πηδάλιον (pēdálion).

parole.significato: any jellyfish of the Pelagia taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Pelagia, derived from Ancient Greek πελάγιος (pelágios, “of the sea”), derived from πέλαγος (pélagos, “sea”).

parole.significato: any of voles of the subgenus Microtus (Pitymys)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Pitymys, derived from Ancient Greek πίτυς (pítus, “pine”) + μῦς (mûs, “mouse, rat”).

parole.significato: any of the taxonomic genus Plocamium of algae
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Plocamium, derived from Ancient Greek πλόκαμος (plókamos, “tress”).

parole.significato: poa
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Poa, from Ancient Greek πόα (póa, “fodder”).

parole.significato: any member of the Polistes taxonomic genus
parole.testo: From translingual Polistes, from Ancient Greek πολιστής (polistḗs, “city-founder”).

parole.significato: scolopacid (member of the Scolopacidae taxonomic family)
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Scolopacidae, derived from the name of the genus Scolopax, from Ancient Greek σκολόπαξ (skolópax, “woodcock”).

parole.significato: any fungus of the genus Stereum
parole.testo: From translingual Stereum, from Ancient Greek στερεός (stereós, “firm, solid”).

parole.significato: any nematode of the Thelazia taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Thelazia, from Ancient Greek θηλάζω (thēlázō, “to suck”).

parole.significato: hartwort
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Tordylium, from Ancient Greek τορδύλιον (tordúlion).

parole.significato: stargazer (perciform fish in the family Uranoscopidae)
parole.testo: From translingual Uranoscopus, from Ancient Greek οὐρᾰνός (ourănós, “sky, heaven”) + σκοπός (skopós, “gazer”). By surface analysis, urano- + -scopo.

parole.significato: the Xerus taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Xerus, from Ancient Greek ξηρός (xērós, “dry; lean”).

parole.significato: xiphosauran
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Xiphosura, from Ancient Greek ξῐ́φος (xĭ́phos) + οὐρά (ourá). By surface analysis, xifo- + -uro.

parole.significato: any beetle of the Zabrus taxonomic genus
parole.testo: Borrowed from translingual Zabrus, from Ancient Greek ζαβρός (zabrós, “voracious”).
